root_cause_label: Agent uses qcow2 disk format instead of raw, omits unattended install setup, never verifies Windows XP reached the login screen, and prematurely declares success based purely on infrastructure service availability.
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent creates a qcow2 disk (instead of the expected raw format), launches QEMU without an unattended install configuration, and prematurely declares task completion after verifying only that infrastructure services (VNC, noVNC, nginx) are listening, without ever confirming Windows XP is installed and at the login screen with tb-admin created.
t_err_evidence: Step 5 executes 'qemu-img create -f qcow2 /app/isos/xp.img 20G', creating the disk in qcow2 format. The reference solution expects a raw disk whose MBR/NTFS signatures can be checked directly; a qcow2 container breaks those low-level byte checks. Additionally, the agent makes no plan for unattended installation (winnt.sif + $OEM$) to guarantee a tb-admin account.
t_commit_evidence: After step 5, the agent builds the entire subsequent plan on top of the qcow2 disk and never revisits disk format or unattended install; all later steps are verification of infrastructure (VNC, nginx, noVNC) that would not fix the wrong-format disk or the missing installation-completion requirement. The trajectory is locked into failure from this point.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacks domain knowledge about two requirements: (1) the test suite verifies installation state via raw-disk byte checks (MBR/NTFS signatures), so a qcow2 disk is incompatible; and (2) an unattended install configuration (winnt.sif / $OEM$ answer file) is needed to create the tb-admin administrator account and guarantee XP reaches the login screen without human interaction. Without this knowledge, the agent treats infrastructure service availability as sufficient proof of task completion.
